check.version_caveat: The mirror is the exact target version (v4.66, Zenodo 14043031; file names, README and prep script all stamp v4.66; the 625/432 reference-point counts reproduce the official Zenodo description exactly), but it is a DERIVED extract, not the official DBdata[asmt][v4.66].RData: (1) it contains only timeseries_values_views (one preferred series per stock from the most recent assessment), not the full 'timeseries' table with all assessments, nor the stock/assessment/bioparams tables; (2) four stocks (HADNS, HERR30, HERRNS, SOLEIIIa) were dropped by the author as empty/non-consecutive, so the official stock count is inferred as 1,442 and must be verified; (3) 156 SST-only stockids were added by a full join and were excluded from all counts here; (4) TBbest covers 475 stocks vs TB 500 -- the official TBbest definition and why 25 TB stocks lack TBbest must be checked in the v4.66 documentation; (5) units/scaling per stock and the 'mdl' (Extended) record were not inspected; (6) no version newer than v4.66 was visible in search results, but the Zenodo community should be checked directly. All counts above should be re-run on the official RAMLDB v4.66.zip (Zenodo, blocked from this sandbox) before preregistration.
check.implications_for_census_projection: Number of systems with >=30 annual observations (verified on the v4.66 mirror): 357 stocks on TBbest (all non-salmon), 362 on TB, 639 on SSB (420 excluding Pacific salmon), 707 on TB-or-SSB (488 excluding Pacific salmon). Of the 357 TBbest>=30 stocks, 292 also have B/BMSY and 272 have both B/BMSY and U/UMSY, so a state-relative-to-reference baseline is available for roughly 80%. Follow-up completeness: TBbest series have a median last year of 2015 (only 151 of 475 end >=2018, 60 end >=2020), so with a 5-year horizon the last usable forecast origin is typically ~2010, and most series end 2012-2018 -- this constrains the number of origins with complete follow-up more than the 30-year length rule does. Collapse-event projection under the 20%-of-max-trailing-5-year-median definition: 117 of 357 TBbest>=30 stocks (33%) have at least one event, but first events are old (median 1994): only 76 first events fall after 1990 and 45 after 2000; because a prequential design needs a training window before each origin (e.g. >=15-20 years), the usable first-collapse pool on TBbest is on the order of ~45-76 events, ~60-114 on non-salmon SSB, and ~91-139 on non-salmon TB-or-SSB. Pacific salmon (358 SSB stocks; 178 of 219 >=30-year series flagged; all series end before 2015) would dominate the event count if pooled and should be treated as a separate biological system stratum or excluded in the primary analysis. Regional grouping is feasible: 18 regions have TBbest>=30 stocks, but several have <=10 (Mediterranean-Black Sea 6, Indian Ocean 6, Pacific 9, Other 2). Published comparators are consistent in scale: Rocha et al. (v4.44) found 479 stocks with series, 373 with >25 years, and 119 (31%) below 50% of historical average; Pélissié et al. 2026 used 315 stocks; Pinsky & Byler 154; Free et al. 235. No EWS-outcome associations were computed.

check.overlap_with_other_sources: RAM Legacy is the common substrate for most of the closest prior work: Pélissié et al. 2026 (315 stocks; their repo used v4.61), Cano et al. 2025 (RAM plus ICES and FishGlob survey CPUE; RAM stock count not visible), Rocha et al. manuscript (v4.44; 479/373 stocks), Hilborn et al. 2020 (882/635 stocks), Free et al. 2019 (235 populations), Pinsky & Byler 2015 (154 populations, v1.0), Zhang 2020 (productivity regime shifts; not re-searched). Overlap with the study's other candidate sources: many RAM assessments (especially the 209 EU and 30 Europe non-EU stocks) are built on ICES survey indices, so RAM biomass and FishGlob/ICES survey series for the same stock are not independent systems and should be grouped by stock/species-area rather than by database (inferred from the region composition; not verified stock-by-stock). RAM's 373 Pacific salmon stocks (spawner counts) may overlap with salmon populations in GPDD/LPD (not verified). OHI (v2025) uses the same v4.66 B/Bmsy fields (476-501 stocks) for a different purpose.

agreements.note: assessid in this file is the stock-boundary-database assessment id (end years up to 2021), not the v4.66 assessment behind timeseries_values_views; it cannot be used to verify the most-recent-assessment convention. The one-series-per-stock property rests on the prep script's use of timeseries_values_views, which is visible in 00-prepare_data.R, and is consistent with the absence of duplicate (stockid, year) rows.

method_concerns: Running-max NaN propagation: the previous collapse code used pandas rolling(5).median().cummax().shift(1); cummax leaves NaN at NaN positions, so for the 5 years after any internal gap the threshold is undefined and events there are missed or delayed. Affects gapped series only: 1 TBbest/TB stock (PANDALSMA18-19) and 8 salmon SSB stocks; changes any-length totals by 1 (TBbest, TB), 4 (SSB), 6 (SSB-or-TB) and the SSB >=30 count by 1 (349 -> 350). No non-salmon >=30 count changes. Recommend an explicit running maximum over all prior valid medians (as in recheck_v466.py) and prespecifying gap handling.

Row-wise TB/SSB coalescing produces hybrid series: B_any = TB where present else SSB splices SSB rows into 180 stocks that have both series (160 with >=30 obs). Because SSB is generally lower than TB, the switch appears as a drop: 35 of the row-coalesce first events land on an SSB-sourced year immediately after TB-sourced years. Under a stock-level rule (TB for the whole stock if any TB, else SSB) the >=30 collapse count falls from 377 to 340 (non-salmon 198 -> 161) and the >=30 denominator from 707 to 696. Any 'SSB-or-TB' analysis should choose one series per stock, never per row.

The assessid column is not RAM assessment metadata: it comes from the HadISST/stock-boundary table joined by the mirror author (present for only 585 of 1,438 RAM stocks, end years <= 2021). It cannot verify the 'most recent assessment per stock' convention; that property is only inferable from the prep script's use of timeseries_values_views. The official DBdata[asmt][v4.66].RData 'timeseries' and 'assessment' tables are needed to confirm it.

Non-annual and gapped series are counted as stocks and toward >=N-year thresholds because n = number of distinct years with a value: 19 SSB series (all pink salmon) are strictly biennial and 1 TBbest/TB series (SRAKEROCKGA, 15 obs at 2-3 yr steps) is strictly non-annual; 100 SSB, 10 TBbest and 11 TB series have internal gaps. Such series can never be flagged by the 5-consecutive-year median rule, so they inflate denominators; prespecify whether length means observations, span or longest consecutive run.

Zero values: 15 SSB stocks contain exact zeros (14 Pacific salmon + URAYVIIde) and 7 SSB first-collapse events fall on a zero; treating zeros as missing changes SSB any-length hits 444 -> 442 and >=30 hits 350 -> 348. TBbest and TB have no zeros or negatives. Decide in advance whether zero escapement is a true observation or missing.

TBbest length histogram: the previous top bin [80,200) omitted the 208-year ATHAL5YZ series (histogram summed to 474, not 475); correct [80+) count is 54. Also, the 1800 start of the year range is this single stock.

The inferred official stock count of 1,442 (1,438 + 4 dropped ids) is not checkable from the file; the prep-script comment says the 4 dropped ids had empty data, so the count of stocks with >=1 value may be 1,438 in the official file too.

Version stamp rests on file names, README text and the prep script only; the extract carries no internal RAM version field. Counts for 625/432 reference-point stocks match the search-engine summary of Zenodo record 14043031 (v4.66), which supports but does not prove that the extract was built from v4.66. The official file remains blocked from this sandbox.

Quantile convention: first/last-year quantiles were reported as integers; the 95% first-year quantile is 1999.3 under linear interpolation (1999 with method='lower'). Minor, but prespecify the quantile method.

Salmon splits are robust: FisheryType == 'Pacific Salmon' and region labels containing '(Pacific Salmon)' identify exactly the same 373 stocks; no Pacific-salmon stock has TBbest or TB, and salmon SSB series end by 2005.

check.version_caveat: Target is the LPR 2024 public release (1970-2020, confidential records removed; release date not visible in search results). All mirrors found are older and were not used: LPR 2016 public CSV in rlpi/figshare, Feb 2016 extract (Daskalova), 09 Sept 2020 download (Buschke), LPR 2022 dataset on Wolfram. The 'almost 42,000 populations / 5,579 species' and the 6-10-year modal length figures come from ZSL's whole-database stats (undated document; includes ~18% confidential records), NOT from the public release; the index itself uses 34,836 populations. On the official download the human must re-verify: release/version stamp, number of populations, per-population observation counts (>=20/25/30/35), mean/median length, fullness (fraction of gap years within span), whether a Data_source/Citation column exists and how many rows cite GPDD/NERC Centre for Population Biology, and the overlap with RAM Legacy/ICES survey series and the North American BBS.
check.implications_for_census_projection: Published evidence says most LPD series are short (modal 6-10 years; >2,000 series at the 2-year minimum; Leung 2020 lost 52% of series with a 10-point minimum), while only 'more than 2,000' records span 1970 to 2011-2015. Hence the number of populations with >=30 ANNUAL OBSERVATIONS is expected to be a small minority of the ~35k public populations - plausibly on the order of low thousands, and fewer than the number with a >=30-year span because 'fullness' (gaps) is incomplete and lower fullness is associated with declining series (Toszogyova 2024). A large share of the long series is expected to come from a few monitoring programmes (BBS named explicitly; GPDD-sourced records not quantified), so effective independent systems are fewer than raw counts and system-level grouping/de-duplication against GPDD, RAM Legacy and ICES will be needed. For collapse-event projection: no published count of LPD populations with >=80% declines was found; the nearest published figures (Leung 2020: <3% of populations drive the index decline, ~1% in extreme-decline clusters) are trend-cluster shares, not threshold-crossing counts, so the expected number of first-collapse events among long, gap-tolerant series cannot be projected from the literature and must be computed from the official download. No EWS-outcome associations were computed or inferred.
check.human_action_required: 1) Register at https://www.livingplanetindex.org/data_portal, state intended use, accept the data-use agreement, and download the current public release; record the release date/version stamp shown at download and the row count. 2) From that file compute: observations per population (columns X1950..X2020), counts with >=20/25/30/35 non-missing annual values, mean/median length and span, fullness (share of gap years within span), and the number of rows whose Data_source/Citation/Source fields mention 'GPDD', 'Global Population Dynamics Database' or 'NERC Centre for Population Biology'. 3) Open https://livingplanetindex.org/documents/LPR2024_Technical_Supplement.pdf and https://www.livingplanetindex.org/documents/database_stats.pdf (both blocked here) to extract the exact population/species counts, the Figure-5 length histogram bins, and any GPDD/source statements. 4) Do not use the rlpi/figshare LPR2016 CSV, the Wolfram LPR2022 mirror, or any other redistributed copy. 5) Note that derived outputs (e.g. per-series collapse labels) may be shared only under the same LPD terms.

check.version_caveat: The computed counts come from a June-2021 BioTIME v1 metadata export (417 studies) mirrored in a collaborator's repository, NOT from BioTIME 2.0 (708 studies, Zenodo v4 of 15 April 2025). The mirror is not byte-identical to the official June-2021 Zenodo file (extra MIN_SAMPLE/AREA columns, missing LICENSE column, 417 vs 381 studies in the public query of the same date), so treat its counts as a lower bound for v2 with these qualifications: (a) v2 added roughly 300 studies and removed 16 v1 studies; (b) v2 re-curation may have changed START_YEAR/END_YEAR/DATA_POINTS for continuing programmes (e.g., extended end years to 2023) and split or merged studies (curation scripts named 'study200_split', 'recurate108' exist in bioTIMEHub/BioTIME); (c) DATA_POINTS counts distinct years, not 'years under a constant protocol' — protocol constancy is a study-inclusion criterion but within-study effort varies and must be handled by rarefaction; (d) species x site series counts require the raw query file (biotime_v2_query_15April25.rds) and a grain decision. Everything must be re-verified on the official Zenodo v4 release (record 15222193): recompute DATA_POINTS/span thresholds for all 708 studies, read the per-study LICENSE column, and check the unverified 'median span 19 years / 12 sampling years' statement against the GEB paper full text (all publisher/repository hosts were egress-blocked here).
check.implications_for_census_projection: Using the v1-lineage mirror as a floor: only 50 of 417 studies have >= 30 sampled years (22 of them gap-free), 27 have >= 35, 101 have >= 20; by realm the >= 30-year studies are Marine 19, Terrestrial 23, Freshwater 8, and by taxon they concentrate in Birds (11), Fish (10), Terrestrial invertebrates (6), Marine invertebrates (5), Terrestrial plants (4). Because BioTIME is assemblage-level, the unit for the census (species x site/cell annual series with >= 30 observations) must be derived from the raw records; the number of such series could be large in the long marine trawl programmes (hundreds of species x many ~96 km2 cells) but these are exactly the ICES DATRAS, NEFSC and DFO surveys that also underlie FishGlob and RAM Legacy, so they should be de-duplicated or treated as one biological system per survey rather than as independent BioTIME systems. Realistic independent contribution from BioTIME 2.0 to the >= 30-annual-observation pool is therefore a few dozen studies (v1 floor 50; v2 total unknown but the 2.0 additions are largely recent, shorter programmes, and no v2 duration distribution was visible), of which only the gap-free ones (22 in v1) satisfy strictly annual sampling without imputation. Sampling effort per year (NUMBER_OF_SAMPLES, SAMPLE_DESC per event) and grain (GRAIN_SIZE_TEXT, AREA_SQ_KM) are provided, so effort-standardised annual abundance series are constructible. Overlap with LPD/GPDD is 'partial' and includes named programmes (North American BBS study 195, Christmas Bird Count 593, Rothamsted 293, Skokholm 46); overlap with FishGlob is substantial for the 31 trawl/survey fish studies. No collapse-event count is projected here: per the hard rules, collapse frequencies and EWS-outcome associations were not computed, and the collapse projection should be re-derived only after the v2 series census is built from the official release.
check.human_action_required: 1) Download biotime_v2_metadata_15April25.csv (and, for the series census, biotime_v2_query_15April25.rds) from Zenodo record 15222193 (blocked from this sandbox) and rerun the saved script logic on all 708 studies: counts of studies with DATA_POINTS >= 20/25/30/35 and with DATA_POINTS == END_YEAR-START_YEAR+1 (gap-free), by REALM and TAXA. 2) Read the per-study LICENSE column and decide whether CC-BY-NC / ODbL studies are admissible for the project's outputs. 3) Derive species x cell annual series from the query file (gridding at ~96 km2 per BioTIMEr defaults, sample-based rarefaction) and count those with >= 30 annual observations under one SAMPLE_DESC_NAME/protocol. 4) Verify in the GEB paper full text (10.1111/geb.70003) the duration distribution and the unverified 'median span 19 years / 12 sampling years' sentence. 5) Build a de-duplication table matching BioTIME TITLE/DATA_SOURCE against the FishGlob survey list (29 surveys), RAM Legacy survey indices and LPD/GPDD source citations before counting independent systems. 6) Optionally confirm the repository licence of gndaskalova/GlobalChangeSpace if the mirrored file is to be redistributed rather than merely used for a sanity check.

method_concerns: Provenance/composition (most important): the collaborator README states ~92% of its BioTIME studies are in the published database and ~8% were 'used with permission'. 8% of 417 is about 33, close to the 417 vs 381 gap the previous agent noted. So this 417-row table is the GlobalChangeSpace authors' working copy including non-public studies, not the public June-2021 release, and the non-public studies cannot be identified from the file (no LICENSE column). Counts are therefore neither exact v1-public figures nor clean lower bounds for v2 without qualification.

Gap-free definition: two studies (249 and 421) have DATA_POINTS greater than the year span, contradicting the 'distinct years' definition; the strict equality test counts them as gapped. Using DATA_POINTS >= span gives 226 gap-free studies (vs 224) and changes only the >=10 (117 -> 118) and >=20 (45 -> 46) gap-free counts. Either START/END_YEAR or DATA_POINTS is wrong for those rows.

START_YEAR/END_YEAR reliability: 17 studies whose titles contain a year range disagree with the metadata years (e.g. 125 'MARMAP Chevron Trap Survey 1990-2009' has START 1988/END 2000; all six MARMAP studies 125, 126, 127, 211, 212, 252 are titled '1990-2009' but carry 1973-2000 metadata years). Span-based thresholds inherit this uncertainty.

'Populated' effort fields: GRAIN_SQ_KM is exactly 0 for 213 of 417 studies and AREA_SQ_KM is 0 for 6, so non-null does not mean usable. The non-standard AREA column differs from AREA_SQ_KM in 236 rows and should be ignored.
Keyword inflation: the fisheries-survey regex includes the generic word 'survey', so 31 includes about 10 reef-transect, trap-survey and observer-programme studies; 21 match without 'survey'.

Category drift between versions: the BioTIMEr 2.0-era subset labels TAXA differently (e.g. 'Plants' where the mirror says 'Terrestrial plants'), so the by-TAXA breakdown cannot be transferred directly to BioTIME 2.0.

Unit of analysis: all counts are per study (one row per STUDY_ID, no duplicates found), not per population/species-by-site series; the prequential design's unit cannot be counted from metadata. RAM-style pitfalls (assessment vs stock, SSB vs biomass) do not apply to this file.

Minor parsing points that do not change any statistic: the file is UTF-8 with one en-dash (a latin-1 read mangles only that title); 'NA' is a literal string in ABUNDANCE_TYPE (46) and BIOMASS_TYPE (305) and pandas maps it to NaN; AB_BIO's single NA is an empty field; study 522's TITLE contains embedded CRLF newlines (wc -l overcounts). Studies 465 and 548 are flagged AB_BIO='B' yet have ABUNDANCE_TYPE='Count' and no BIOMASS_TYPE.

Verification scope: no WebSearch queries were issued; the single network call was to raw.githubusercontent.com (an allowed host) and confirmed byte-identity with the upstream master file. The claims about Zenodo record 5026943 contents (381 studies, column set) and about BioTIME 2.0 (708 studies) were not re-verifiable here because those hosts are egress-blocked.
